entities.name: Zika Virus
entities.description: An acute mosquito-borne arboviral disease caused by Zika virus (flavivirus), characterized by a mild self-limiting illness with low-grade fever, pruritic maculopapular exanthem, bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, and migratory polyarthralgia, with critical potential for severe neurotropic and teratogenic complications including Guillain-Barré syndrome and Congenital Zika Syndrome.

entities.name: Diurnal Aedes Mosquito Bite (Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus)
entities.description: Bite inoculations from infected female daytime-biting mosquitoes belonging to the Aedes genus (primarily Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus), with peak biting activity occurring during early morning and late afternoon.

entities.name: Unprotected Sexual Contact with Infected Partner
entities.description: Secondary non-vector sexual transmission of Zika virus through unprotected vaginal, anal, or oral sex due to prolonged shedding of infectious viral particles in semen (up to several months post-infection), vaginal fluids, and saliva.

entities.name: Transplacental Vertical Transmission During Pregnancy
entities.description: In utero maternal-to-fetal transmission occurring across any gestational trimester, crossing the placental barrier to infect fetal neural progenitor cells and conferring significant risk of severe embryopathy.

entities.name: Blood Transfusion or Organ Transplantation Exposure
entities.description: Iatrogenic hematogenous or tissue-mediated transmission through transfusion of contaminated, unscreened blood products or transplantation of infected donor organs.

entities.name: Travel to or Residence in Zika Endemic Tropical Regions
entities.description: Epidemiological exposure through travel to or residence in tropical and subtropical regions of the Americas, Caribbean, Pacific Islands, Southeast Asia, or Africa with established active Aedes transmission.

entities.name: Zika Virus (ZIKV Flavivirus)
entities.description: An enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA arbovirus belonging to the genus Flavivirus within the family Flaviviridae, closely related to Spondweni virus and dengue virus, possessing neurotropic and fetotropic pathogenicity.

entities.name: Mild Non-Spiking Low-Grade Fever (37.5°C–38.5°C)
entities.description: Mild, non-spiking elevation of core body temperature typically between 37.5°C and 38.5°C, self-limiting within 2 to 7 days or occasionally completely absent (subclinical/afebrile), lacking the rigors of malaria or high continuous fever of dengue.

entities.name: Pruritic Centrifugal Maculopapular Exanthem
entities.description: Erythematous, punctate, finely maculopapular and notably pruritic skin eruption appearing early (day 1–2) on the face and spreading centrifugally to the trunk, extremities, palms, and soles over several days.

entities.name: Bilateral Non-Purulent Conjunctival Hyperemia
entities.description: Diffuse injection of bulbar and palpebral conjunctivae occurring bilaterally without purulent exudate, eyelid crusting, or photophobia, appearing early in the symptomatic phase.

entities.name: Migratory Polyarthralgia with Periarticular Edema
entities.description: Mild to moderate migratory joint pain predominantly involving small peripheral joints of the hands, wrists, knees, and ankles, accompanied by soft-tissue periarticular edema or tenosynovitis without joint destruction.

entities.name: Congenital Microcephaly and Intracranial Calcifications
entities.description: Severe intrauterine neurodevelopmental disruption in neonates presenting with disproportionate microcephaly, corticomedullary subcortical calcifications, ventriculomegaly, simplified gyral pattern, chorioretinal atrophy, and arthrogryposis (Congenital Zika Syndrome).

entities.name: Post-Infectious Guillain-Barré Syndrome Ascending Paralysis
entities.description: Acute post-infectious autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy manifesting 1 to 3 weeks following acute Zika illness, characterized by progressive symmetrical ascending flaccid weakness, hyporeflexia/areflexia, and potential respiratory compromise.

entities.name: Normal or Mildly Depressed Leukocyte Count without Severe Leukopenia
entities.description: Triage complete blood count showing normal or mild leukopenia (total WBC 3,500–5,000/µL), lacking the profound leukopenia (<2,000/µL) frequently seen in acute severe dengue.

entities.name: Mild Thrombocytopenia without Severe Platelet Depletion
entities.description: Peripheral platelet counts demonstrating normal levels or mild thrombocytopenia (typically 100,000–150,000/µL), with severe thrombocytopenia (<50,000/µL) being exceptionally rare in uncomplicated infection.

entities.name: Normal Hematocrit with Absence of Hemoconcentration or Plasma Leakage
entities.description: Admission baseline hematocrit values showing normal stability without hemoconcentration (hematocrit increase ≥ 20%), capillary hyperpermeability, or plasma leakage.

entities.name: Normal Bedside POCUS without Serosal Effusion or Gallbladder Wall Thickening
entities.description: Point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) demonstrating normal liver, spleen, and gallbladder wall architecture, with complete absence of ascites, pleural effusions, or pericardial fluid.

entities.name: Zika Virus RNA Detection via RT-PCR in Acute Serum or Urine
entities.description: Confirmatory molecular diagnostic detection of Zika viral RNA by reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in acute-phase serum (within 10–11 days of symptom onset) or urine.

entities.name: Severe Plasma Leakage, Hemoconcentration, or Hypovolemic Shock
entities.description: Presence of objective plasma leakage signs including pleural effusions, ascites, hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise ≥ 20%), narrow pulse pressure, or hypovolemic shock, which definitively rules out uncomplicated Zika virus.

entities.name: Profound Thrombocytopenia (<50,000/µL) with Spontaneous Hemorrhage
entities.description: Platelet counts dropping below 50,000/µL, spontaneous petechiae, ecchymoses, or mucosal bleeding, which effectively excludes uncomplicated Zika virus infection.

entities.name: Crippling Symmetrical Polyarthritis with Inability to Ambulate
entities.description: Incapacitating, severe inflammatory polyarthritis preventing ambulation or hand flexion with prolonged morning stiffness, which points to Chikungunya rather than Zika virus.

entities.name: Purulent Conjunctival Exudate with Photophobia
entities.description: Presence of thick purulent or mucopurulent ocular discharge, matting of eyelids, or marked photophobia, which rules out Zika non-purulent conjunctivitis in favor of bacterial or adenoviral conjunctivitis.

entities.name: Prolonged High Fever Exceeding 7 Days
entities.description: High continuous or spiking fever persisting beyond 7 days, which is incompatible with the typically mild, self-limiting 2–7 day febrile course of acute Zika virus.

entities.name: Prominent Respiratory Symptoms (Cough, Coryza) or Koplik Spots
entities.description: Presence of pronounced upper or lower respiratory symptoms including persistent cough, purulent coryza, or pathognomonic mucosal Koplik spots, ruling out Zika virus in favor of measles or common respiratory infections.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, characterized by high continuous fever (>39°C), severe retro-orbital headache, prostrating myalgia/bone pain, profound thrombocytopenia (<50,000/µL), and risks of plasma leakage and dengue shock syndrome.

entities.name: Chikungunya Virus Disease
entities.description: Alphavirus infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with sudden high-spiking fever and crippling, severe, symmetrical polyarthritis predominantly affecting peripheral small joints, frequently persisting chronically for months to years.

entities.name: Measles (Rubeola)
entities.description: Highly contagious paramyxovirus infection presenting with high fevers, the classic triad of cough, coryza, and photophobic conjunctivitis, followed by pathognomonic Koplik spots and a cephalocaudal maculopapular rash.

entities.name: Rubella (German Measles)
entities.description: Togavirus infection presenting with mild fever, fine pink maculopapular rash, and prominent tender retroauricular, suboccipital, and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, without marked conjunctivitis or mosquito vector transmission.

entities.name: Parvovirus B19 Infection
entities.description: Erythrovirus infection presenting in children with an erythematous 'slapped-cheek' facial rash and reticular body exanthem, or in adult females with acute symmetric polyarthropathy mimicking rheumatoid arthritis, without tropical vector exposure.

entities.name: Acetaminophen Symptomatic Analgesia and Antipyresis
entities.description: First-line oral acetaminophen (paracetamol) therapy providing effective symptomatic reduction of mild fever, headache, and peripheral arthralgias, avoiding platelet dysfunction before dengue is excluded.

entities.name: Oral Second-Generation Antihistamines for Pruritus Relief
entities.description: Oral second-generation H1-receptor antagonists (e.g., cetirizine, loratadine) providing targeted symptomatic relief for the pruritic component of the maculopapular rash.

entities.name: Supportive Fluid Hydration and Rest
entities.description: Conservative clinical management with adequate oral fluid replenishment and rest leading to spontaneous disease resolution within 2 to 7 days, as no specific antiviral therapy exists.

entities.name: Empirical Antibacterial Therapy Refractoriness
entities.description: Intrinsic unresponsiveness to empirical broad-spectrum antibacterial agents (beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, macrolides), confirming a non-bacterial, viral etiology.

relationships.target: Diurnal Aedes Mosquito Bite (Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus)
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Primarily transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female diurnal Aedes mosquitoes (Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus) active during early morning and late afternoon hours.

relationships.target: Unprotected Sexual Contact with Infected Partner
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Transmitted directly between humans via sexual intercourse due to prolonged shedding of replication-competent virus in male semen and female genital tract secretions.
[TRANSMITTED_BY] Transmitted vertically from mother to fetus across the placenta throughout pregnancy, directly infecting embryonic and fetal neuroprogenitor cells.

relationships.target: Blood Transfusion or Organ Transplantation Exposure
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Contracted via direct hematogenous inoculation through transfusion of contaminated, unscreened blood products or transplantation of infected solid organs.

relationships.target: Travel to or Residence in Zika Endemic Tropical Regions
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Contracted via epidemiological exposure during travel to or residence in tropical and subtropical regions across the Americas, Caribbean, Pacific Islands, Southeast Asia, or Africa where Aedes vectors circulate.
[HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused etiologically by Zika virus, an enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the Flavivirus genus within the Flaviviridae family.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Presents classically with mild, non-spiking low-grade fever (37.5°C–38.5°C) lasting 2–7 days, or a completely afebrile subclinical course, contrasting with the high spiking rigors of dengue or malaria.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Manifests as an erythematous, finely maculopapular, intensely pruritic eruption appearing on days 1–2 on the face and rapidly spreading centrifugally to the trunk, limbs, palms, and soles.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features diffuse bilateral bulbar and palpebral conjunctival injection without purulent discharge, eyelid crusting, or photophobia as an early cardinal sign.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Manifests as mild to moderate migratory polyarthralgia primarily targeting small peripheral joints of the hands, wrists, knees, and ankles, accompanied by soft tissue periarticular puffiness without destructive arthritis.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Causes severe teratogenic congenital malformations in infants infected in utero, characterized by severe microcephaly, corticomedullary intracranial calcifications, ventriculomegaly, simplified gyral pattern, chorioretinopathy, and arthrogryposis.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Triggers acute post-infectious autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy 1 to 3 weeks post-infection, leading to progressive ascending symmetrical flaccid weakness, hyporeflexia, and potential respiratory failure.

relationships.target: Normal or Mildly Depressed Leukocyte Count without Severe Leukopenia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission laboratory profile demonstrates normal or mildly decreased total leukocyte count (3,500–5,000/µL), notably lacking marked leukopenia (<2,000/µL).

relationships.target: Mild Thrombocytopenia without Severe Platelet Depletion
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows normal or only mildly reduced platelet counts (100,000–150,000/µL); drop below 50,000/µL is exceptionally rare in uncomplicated infection.

relationships.target: Normal Hematocrit with Absence of Hemoconcentration or Plasma Leakage
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Preserves stable baseline hematocrit without evidence of vascular hyperpermeability, hemoconcentration, or plasma leakage.

relationships.target: Normal Bedside POCUS without Serosal Effusion or Gallbladder Wall Thickening
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside point-of-care ultrasound reveals completely normal gallbladder wall thickness, liver, and spleen, with absence of pleural effusion, ascites, or pericardial fluid.

relationships.target: Zika Virus RNA Detection via RT-PCR in Acute Serum or Urine
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Confirmed at admission by direct molecular detection of viral RNA via RT-PCR in acute serum (detectable up to 10–11 days from onset) or urine.

relationships.target: Severe Plasma Leakage, Hemoconcentration, or Hypovolemic Shock
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of third-space plasma leakage (pleural effusion, ascites, hemoconcentration with hematocrit increase ≥ 20%), narrow pulse pressure, or hypovolemic shock definitively rules out uncomplicated Zika virus.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Severe platelet count depression (<50,000/µL), spontaneous mucosal hemorrhage, or petechiae completely rules out uncomplicated Zika virus.

relationships.target: Crippling Symmetrical Polyarthritis with Inability to Ambulate
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Severe, crippling, incapacitating polyarthritis that prevents walking or finger flexion with intense morning stiffness rules out Zika virus in favor of Chikungunya.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of copious purulent eye discharge, crusting, pseudomembranes, or severe photophobia rules out the benign non-purulent conjunctival hyperemia of Zika virus.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Prolonged high-grade fever persisting longer than 7 days rules out acute uncomplicated Zika virus infection, which typically subsides within 2 to 7 days.

relationships.target: Prominent Respiratory Symptoms (Cough, Coryza) or Koplik Spots
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Prominent upper or lower respiratory manifestations such as heavy cough, purulent nasal discharge, or pathognomonic Koplik spots rules out Zika virus in favor of measles or acute respiratory virus infections.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Dengue Fever, which causes high continuous/biphasic fever (>39°C), severe retro-orbital headache, profound thrombocytopenia (<50,000/µL), hemoconcentration, and life-threatening plasma leakage/shock, whereas Zika presents with low-grade fever, pruritic maculopapular rash, and non-purulent conjunctivitis without plasma leak.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Chikungunya Virus Disease, which presents with sudden high-spiking fever and incapacitating, severe, symmetrical polyarthritis predominantly affecting peripheral small joints that frequently persists for months to years, compared to Zika's mild transient polyarthralgia and non-purulent conjunctivitis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Measles, which manifests with high fever, prominent triad of cough, coryza, and photophobic conjunctivitis, and buccal Koplik spots, all of which are absent in Zika virus.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Rubella, which features prominent tender retroauricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy and lacks the intense conjunctival injection and mosquito vector transmission profile of Zika virus.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Parvovirus B19, which causes classic slapped-cheek facial rash in children or symmetric rheumatoid-like polyarthropathy in adult women without tropical mosquito vector exposure or conjunctivitis.
[RESPONDS_TO] Symptomatically responsive to oral acetaminophen (paracetamol) for alleviation of low-grade fever and mild joint pain; preferred initial analgesic while awaiting exclusion of dengue.

relationships.target: Oral Second-Generation Antihistamines for Pruritus Relief
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Symptomatically responsive to oral second-generation H1-receptor antagonists (cetirizine, loratadine) for effective relief of the pruritic maculopapular rash.
[RESPONDS_TO] Clinically responsive to conservative supportive care with oral fluid replenishment and rest, spontaneously resolving over 2 to 7 days in uncomplicated cases.
[INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Intrinsically unresponsive to empirical broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens (such as beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, or macrolides) due to its viral etiology.
